rows.definition: gateway.adjudicationOutcomeSignal enum value meaning EVERY proposed tool call in a served turn was denied by adjudication, so no call survived to be executed or served back to the model.
rows.distinction: It is the ALL-DENIED classification a served turn folds to - NOT the partial case, where some calls were kept - unlike adjudicationOutcomeToolFeedback, which fires when at least one call survives.

rows.definition: gateway.adjudicationOutcomeForTurn is the pure classifier function that folds one served turn's []ToolAdjudication plus its kept/served call counts into a single adjudicationOutcomeSignal.
rows.distinction: It is the FUNCTION that computes the outcome, not the enum value it returns - unlike adjudicationOutcomeSignal, the type of the value it produces.

rows.definition: gateway.adjudicationOutcomeSignal is the int-enum TYPE (reset / deny-all / tool-feedback) that classifies a served turn's overall adjudication shape for the exit-summary counters.
rows.distinction: It is the ENUM TYPE itself, not the fold that produces a value of it - unlike adjudicationOutcomeForTurn, the function that classifies one turn into this type.

rows.definition: gateway.adjudicationOutcomeSignal enum value meaning some proposed calls were denied but at least one call was kept and served, so the model receives real tool-result feedback this turn.
rows.distinction: It is the PARTIAL-deny outcome - NOT the all-denied case - unlike adjudicationOutcomeDenyAll, where nothing survived to serve.

rows.definition: devcmd.RunCIPreflight is the `fak-dev ci-preflight` entrypoint that archives a requested committed ref into an isolated temporary checkout and reports whether that tip is gofmt-clean and build-green, without reading peer-dirty working-tree files.
rows.distinction: It checks the git TIP's build health, not whether a dispatch worker may spawn or one tool call is admitted - unlike DispatchPreflight (dispatch admission) and the preflight ladder (per-call schema checks).

rows.definition: dispatchtick.EvaluatePreflight is the pure fold (state in, PreflightResult out) over a PreflightInput - max-workers, dos target, host capacity, seat-pool terms - that decides whether dispatch may admit another worker this tick.
rows.distinction: It is the PURE decision fold dispatch admission calls each tick, not the git-tip build-health check (ci-preflight) or livecodebench's own host-state observation (PreflightProbe).

rows.definition: compute.KVEvictPolicy is the enum (KVEvictLRU / KVEvictCostAware) selecting which victim-ranking policy ReplayKVCache and the offline KV-replay tooling simulate when replaying recorded KV events against a token budget.
rows.distinction: It is the OFFLINE replay/simulation eviction policy compute scores admission decisions against, not radixkv's live EvictionPolicy the running server actually enforces - unlike PolicyEvictions (radixkv), the counter for the live tree's policy-driven drops.

rows.definition: cmd/fak's policyBytes is the raw JSON byte slice of the guard's admission-policy file (or the embedded default) read at guard startup, before policy.ParseRuntime compiles it and guardPolicyDigest hashes it.
rows.distinction: It is the RAW on-disk bytes captured at read time, not the digest computed from them or the compiled decision table - unlike PolicyDigest (guard spawn provenance), the hash of these same bytes, and Policy (loaded), the compiled table.

rows.definition: resume.PostureWarmHit ("warm_hit") is the Posture enum value for a CROSS-SESSION warm hit (#940) - a resume that opened straight onto a warm cache carried over from a PRIOR session, not merely warm within the current one.
rows.distinction: It is a resume-cache readiness value, not the tool-admission default-deny posture or the adjudicator's secret-discovery posture - unlike posture (tool admission) and SecretPosture (adjudicator), which govern call/result admission, not cache warmth.

rows.definition: qwen36nodereports's preflightPaths is the glob-matched list of already-written `preflight-*.json` report file paths discovered under a node's report directory, used to detect whether a preflight report exists at all.
rows.distinction: It is a discovered list of FILESYSTEM PATHS to past preflight artifacts, not the in-memory verdict structs a preflight check produces live - unlike PreflightResult (dispatchtick) and PreflightProbe (livecodebench).

rows.definition: livecodebench.PreflightProbe is the observed host state (uv, python, dataset, gateway, sandbox availability) that cmd/livecodebench's preflight build folds into a human-readable readiness report before a run starts.
rows.distinction: It is livecodebench's OWN host-capability observation, unrelated to dispatch's worker-admission fold - unlike EvaluatePreflight (dispatchtick), which decides whether a new worker may spawn this tick.

rows.definition: dispatchtick.PreflightResult is the struct EvaluatePreflight returns - the dispatch tick's admission verdict, spawn-allowed count, blocking reasons, and host-capacity components (its Map() renders it for logging/JSON).
rows.distinction: It is the STRUCTURED verdict WITH components dispatchtick computes locally, not dispatchsweep's PreflightVerdict, a plain recorded string field on a trial/status row.

rows.definition: gateway.prependAdjudicationContentNote takes adjudicationNote's short prose summary of a turn's denies/repairs and splices it onto the front of the assistant message's Content before the response reaches a client that only reads the content channel.
rows.distinction: It SPLICES the note into the returned message body, it does not compose the note text itself - unlike adjudicationNote (gateway), the renderer whose output it prepends.

rows.definition: loopmgr.RestartPolicy is the pure crashloop fence (MaxAttempts, BaseDelay, MaxDelay, ResetAfter) whose Decide/BackoffDelay methods govern a supervised loop's automatic restart/backoff scheduling, reused by cmd/fak's watchdog as watchdogRestartPolicy.
rows.distinction: It governs PROCESS-SUPERVISION backoff after a crash, not tool-call authorization - unlike Policy (loaded) and DefaultPolicy (adjudicator), which decide whether a tool call is allowed.

rows.definition: (*Adjudicator).SecretPolicy is the accessor method that returns the adjudicator's currently active SecretPosture value plus its declared secret-detection regex patterns, read under the policy RLock; normgate and secretgate call it at admit time.
rows.distinction: It is the ACCESSOR METHOD returning the posture plus patterns, not the SecretPosture enum value it returns - unlike SecretPosture (adjudicator) - and it is a different domain than RestartPolicy (loopmgr), an unrelated process-supervision policy.

rows.definition: boundarylint.TestTestSuitePolicy is the enforcement test (a ratchet: only a tell in a file NOT yet grandfathered fails) that walks the repo's test-suite naming/shape family and is reported by `fak boundary`.
rows.distinction: It is the ENFORCEMENT gate over the TEST-SUITE naming/shape family, not a tool-admission or capability policy - unlike Policy (loaded) and RestartPolicy (loopmgr), which govern unrelated domains.

rows.definition: cmd/fak's tPolicy is a time.Now() checkpoint captured immediately before a guard/serve entrypoint (guard_setup.go, guard_startup.go, serve.go) loads and parses its admission policy, later subtracted (time.Since(tPolicy)) to report the policy-load stage duration.
rows.distinction: It is a WALL-CLOCK TIMING checkpoint local variable, not a policy value or struct field - unlike policyBytes, the bytes it times the read of, and radixkv's t.policy field (the tree's live eviction policy), an unrelated receiver-scoped field that happens to normalize to the same token.

rows.definition: "unadjudicated" names an executor or call path that runs WITHOUT going through the adjudicator at all - microagent's toolexec registry refuses (#2018) to ever hand back a bare unadjudicated executor, while livecodebench's raw-arm gateway calls are deliberately run UNADJUDICATED to collect an un-gated baseline.
rows.distinction: It describes the ABSENCE of adjudication on a call path, not a verdict the adjudicator returns - unlike verdict (abi.Verdict) and reason code, which describe what happens once a call IS adjudicated.
